title: A compact space with countably many separating metric-valued maps is metrizable
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a compact topological space, where compact means that every open cover has a finite subcover. For each integer $n\geq0$, let $(Y_n,d_n)$ be a metric space and let $u_n:X\to Y_n$ be continuous. Assume that for every two distinct points $x,x^\prime\in X$ there is $n\geq0$ with $u_n(x)\ne u_n(x^\prime)$. Then $X$ is metrizable: there exists a metric on its underlying set inducing its given topology. Empty $X$ and empty metric targets are allowed; no completeness hypothesis is imposed.
